question: How do the scriptwriter and length-fit steps in .claude/agents/ and docs/ keep narration within the target duration and tie each sentence to cited fact ids in claims?
answer_summary: The scriptwriter sizes each scene with a spoken-word formula (about 145 words per minute, numbers counted as spoken) and lists fact ids in claims for every factual sentence, which check_script.py validates. Because estimates ran short, a length-fit stage measures the real Kokoro voiceover and sends measured per-line seconds back for a trim pass when the total is more than 15% off target. The first run showed the need: 83.8 s measured vs a 60 s target, trimmed to 56.0 s.

facts.claim: The scriptwriter agent must list fact ids in claims for every sentence that states a fact; purely framing sentences get an empty claims list.
facts.excerpt: Every sentence that states a fact must list the fact ids it relies on in `claims`.

facts.claim: The scriptwriter budgets length with a formula: spoken words are counted with numbers said in full, at about 145 spoken words per minute at speed 0.9, with 0.35 s per sentence gap and 1.3 s per scene lead-in and hold.

In the length-fit stage the orchestrator generates the real voiceover and, if the measure is off target (exit 2), sends the scriptwriter measured per-line seconds for a trim pass; at most 2 trim rounds, and only changed lines are re-voiced.
facts.excerpt: After 2 trim rounds, continue even if still off, and note the length in the log.

facts.claim: The first end-to-end run measured 83.8 s of voiceover against a 60 s target (+40%); the trim pass deleted 2 lines and shortened 7, reaching 56.0 s.
facts.source_title: Step 2 Results: Agent Pipeline, First 60-Second Run

facts.claim: The length-fit stage was added because TTS reads numbers in full, so plain word counts underestimated length by about 25%; the trigger is a total more than 15% off target.
facts.source_title: Step 2 Results: Agent Pipeline, First 60-Second Run
facts.excerpt: TTS reads numbers in full, so word counts underestimate length by ~25%.

facts.claim: The tool check_script.py validates scenes.json structure, that every cited fact exists, and estimated length; the scriptwriter must rerun it until it prints PASS.
facts.excerpt: Validates `scenes.json`: structure, every cited fact exists, estimated length.

gaps: Length fit is not a separate agent: it is an orchestrator step (tools/voiceover.py) plus a scriptwriter trim pass.
Did not read tools/*.py code; the 15% threshold comes from README.md and docs/step2-results.md descriptions.
